sentences.text:
....Respondents ORDER:
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Government Pleader appearing for the respondents.

2. This writ petition is filed questioning the acquisition notice issued by the 5th respondent under Section 15(2) read with Rule 21 of the Act under reference No. Gen/A/839/2020 dated 27.06.2020.
3.

The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that under the impugned acquisition notice of the 5th respondent, the petitioner is going to lose the land in an extent of Ac.0.15 cents in R.S.No. 357 situated in Jambhupatnam Village, Korukonda Mandal, East Godavari District.

The petitioner is an agriculturist cultivating the subject land and if the proposed acquisition is made through the middle of the land of the petitioner, the remaining part of the land would become uncultivable and his livelihood will be deprived.
The petitioner has no objection for the acquisition but the reasonableness shall be there on the part of the respondents to acquire the land by paying suitable compensation for it.

sentences.text: On the other hand, the learned Government Pleader submits that the neighbouring land owners agreed for the acquisition and parted with their lands and only the petitioner is objecting for the same.
Whereas the petitioner also gave a letter dated 30.06.2020 to the 5th respondent expressing no objection to take the land for acquisition from the northern side.

5. In view of the above said facts and circumstances, the petitioner is permitted to give a fresh representation to the 5th respondent and the same shall be considered in accordance with law and acquisition proceedings can go on strictly in accordance with law.
6. Accordingly, the writ petition is disposed off.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Interim order granted earlier by this court dated 17.07.2020 is vacated.
As a sequel, Miscellaneous Petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
